Getting started with lantern

Yu Wang

Bjoernar Tuftin

Paul Auer

Source: vignettes/lantern.Rmd
lantern.Rmd

Introduction

In admixed individuals, each stretch of the genome is inherited from one of several ancestral populations. A rare-variant burden test that pools all carriers can miss an effect that exists in only one ancestral background, or wrongly attribute one. lantern uses local ancestry to split each sample’s alternate-allele dosage into per-ancestry dosages (e.g. African and European). It then runs gene-level SMMAT tests (GMMAT) separately for each ancestry and combines the per-ancestry p-values with the Cauchy combination test.

The workflow has three steps:

  1. Split a phased VCF by local ancestry from an RFMix .msp.tsv file with ancestry_split().
  2. Write each ancestry’s dosages to a SeqArray GDS file with write_ancestry_gds().
  3. Test each gene in every ancestry and Cauchy-combine the results with ancestry_smmat().

Installation 

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("lantern")
library(lantern)

lantern reads VCFs with bcftools when it is on PATH, which is fastest and also reads BCF. Otherwise it falls back to SeqArray, so no external tools are needed.

Example data

The package ships a small simulated dataset: 60 admixed samples, 200 rare variants on chromosome 19, two ancestral populations (AFR, EUR) and 8 genes. The phenotype carries an effect that is driven only by African-ancestry alleles in GENE2.

ext <- system.file("extdata", package = "lantern")
vcf <- file.path(ext, "toy.vcf.gz")     # phased genotypes
msp <- file.path(ext, "toy.msp.tsv")    # RFMix local ancestry
substr(readLines(msp, n = 3), 1, 70)
#> [1] "#Subpopulation order/codes: AFR=0\tEUR=1"                                                      
#> [2] "#chm\tspos\tepos\tsgpos\tegpos\tn snps\tS001.0\tS001.1\tS002.0\tS002.1\tS003.0\tS"             
#> [3] "chr19\t1e+06\t4999999\t1.00\t5.00\t25\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t0\t1\t0\t1\t0\t0\t1\t0\t0\t0\t0"

Step 1: split dosages by local ancestry

mode = "haplotype" assigns each phased allele to the ancestry of its own haplotype, so it is exact. mode = "dosage" ignores phase: it splits ambiguous mixed-ancestry heterozygotes using population proportions estimated from the unambiguous carriers, shrunk toward each chromosome arm’s global ancestry. See vignette("split-intuition") for the details.

split <- ancestry_split(vcf, msp, mode = "dosage", chrom = "chr19",
                        verbose = FALSE)
names(split)
#> [1] "AFR"             "EUR"             "variant_info"    "sample_ids"     
#> [5] "mode"            "ancestry_counts" "tract_info"      "overlap"
dim(split$AFR)
#> [1] 184  60
split$AFR[1:4, 1:6]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [2,]    0    0    0    1    0    0
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
split$EUR[1:4, 1:6]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#> [1,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [2,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#> [4,]    0    0    0    0    0    0

The result also records which variants and samples were kept:

head(split$variant_info)
#>   chrom     pos ref alt
#> 1 chr19 1168394   T   A
#> 2 chr19 1240171   T   C
#> 3 chr19 2252809   A   G
#> 4 chr19 2330989   C   T
#> 5 chr19 2436455   A   G
#> 6 chr19 2459485   C   G
split$overlap[c("n_common", "n_variants_kept", "n_monomorphic_filtered")]
#> $n_common
#> [1] 60
#> 
#> $n_variants_kept
#> [1] 184
#> 
#> $n_monomorphic_filtered
#> [1] 16

Step 2: write per-ancestry GDS files 

out_dir <- tempfile("lantern-")
gds <- write_ancestry_gds(split, out_dir, verbose = FALSE)
gds
#> $AFR
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp7eWPFD/lantern-422647e4df14/AFR.gds"
#> 
#> $EUR
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp7eWPFD/lantern-422647e4df14/EUR.gds"

Step 3: ancestry-stratified gene tests

ancestry_smmat() fits the null model once with GMMAT::glmmkin(), then runs GMMAT::SMMAT() on each ancestry’s GDS file. Gene-level weights for the Cauchy combination are the median per-variant carrier counts in each ancestry. The samples here are unrelated, so the kinship matrix is the identity.

pheno <- read.delim(file.path(ext, "toy_pheno.tsv"))
kinship <- diag(nrow(pheno))
dimnames(kinship) <- list(pheno$id, pheno$id)

res <- ancestry_smmat(gds, pheno, y ~ age + sex, kinship,
                      gene_group_file = file.path(ext, "toy_genes.tsv"),
                      ancestry_counts = split$ancestry_counts,
                      variant_info    = split$variant_info,
                      verbose = FALSE)
res$results
#>    gene        p_AFR     p_EUR w_AFR w_EUR     p_cauchy
#> 1 GENE1 8.429637e-01 0.2321365    42     1 8.378715e-01
#> 2 GENE2 1.860597e-08 0.8339380    39     2 1.956013e-08
#> 3 GENE3 5.076218e-01 0.2765924    41     3 4.887590e-01
#> 4 GENE4 3.937408e-01 0.7851541    40     1 4.049334e-01
#> 5 GENE5 2.826767e-01 0.2007261    40     2 2.776638e-01
#> 6 GENE6 6.638040e-01 0.5783176    33     2 6.594389e-01
#> 7 GENE7 1.517208e-01 0.4259828    41     1 1.544780e-01
#> 8 GENE8 6.060560e-01 0.3600061    33     3 5.863210e-01

GENE2 is strongly associated in the AFR test but not in the EUR test, which matches the simulated African-specific effect. A test that pools both ancestries would dilute that signal.
